mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AppendOnlyAuditEntries allows two AuditEntry atoms for the same application to share an identical (entryPrevStatus, entryNewStatus) pair, simulating a duplicate/mutated entry that the append-only invariant forbids. The injection forces exactly that scenario.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.entryApp = e2.entryApp and e1.entryPrevStatus = e2.entryPrevStatus and e1.entryNewStatus = e2.entryNewStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_NoSelfApproval allows a successful PATCH operation where the caller is also the application's applicant. The injection forces an Operation with kind=PatchApplicationStatus, outcome=Success, and opCaller equal to the application's appApplicant, directly violating FR-013.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfApprovalViolation { some op: Operation, a: LoanApplication | op.opKind = PatchApplicationStatus and op.opOutcome = Success and op.opTarget = a and op.opCaller = a.appApplicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_OneInFlightPerApplicant allows two LoanApplication atoms to exist with the same appApplicant and both in a Pending/UnderReview status, violating the one-in-flight invariant from FR-008.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TwoInFlightViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.appApplicant = a2.appApplicant and a1.appStatus = Pending and a2.appStatus = UnderReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AuditEndpointAuditorOnly allows a non-auditor caller (e.g., a pure applicant) to successfully access GetApplicationAudit, leaking audit log existence to non-auditors in violation of FR-023.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditEndpointLeakViolation { some op: Operation | op.opKind = GetApplicationAudit and op.opOutcome = Success and RAuditor not in op.opCaller.userRoles }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_OwnershipBasedAccess permits a pure applicant (no officer, no auditor role) to successfully GET an application they do not own, breaking the byte-equivalent no-leakage guarantee from FR-020/FR-021.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipLeakViolation { some op: Operation, a: LoanApplication | op.opKind = GetApplicationById and op.opOutcome = Success and op.opTarget = a and op.opCaller != a.appApplicant and RAuditor not in op.opCaller.userRoles and ROfficer not in op.opCaller.userRoles }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_OnlyAssignedOfficerCanPatch allows an officer who is NOT the assigned officer to successfully PATCH an application's status, violating the core assignment-control invariant of FR-012.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnassignedOfficerPatchViolation { some op: Operation, a: LoanApplication | op.opKind = PatchApplicationStatus and op.opOutcome = Success and op.opTarget = a and a.assignedOfficer != op.opCaller and ROfficer in op.opCaller.userRoles }
